sites.quote: The IV MUST be unique for each invocation for a particular security association (SA) but does not need to be unpredictable.
The receiver MUST accept any length of padding.
sites.reason: RFC 8247 Section 2.1 grades the cipher SHOULD for IKEv2: "there were not enough IKEv2 implementations supporting ENCR_CHACHA20_POLY1305 to be able to introduce it at the SHOULD+ level". The receiver padding rule binds the IKE SA Encrypted payload, and ze admits ChaCha20-Poly1305 for ESP only (internal/component/ike/crypto/transform.go espOnlyEncryptionRegistry; aeadTransforms gives it no IKE mode). The absent IKE SA use is disclosed on docs/features/rfc-status.md through the Support remaining row of rfc/short/rfc7634.md

sites.quote: As with other AEAD algorithms, INTEG (type 3) transform substructures MUST NOT be specified, or just one INTEG transform MAY be included with value NONE (0).
